svg.text: Ch'alish P'ilam, the common hand — layer 2: the glyphs
Every glyph is built from the strokes of layer 1, in one even line. A glyph is a concept; two or more together make another, the first usually the head and the rest modifying it. Context decides.
Nearly everyone knows the 24 core glyphs, and a few more of their trade. Scribes know many more, the long compounds and the sound of every glyph; priests know the sacred glyphs.
A glyph's sound is the opening consonant and vowel of the word that names it, its catch left out. Drawn from tools/chalish-pilam/glyphs.py.
the world above, the gods and the honoured dead
the world below, the underworld and its trials
Beyond the core: glyphs of a trade, of the scribes, and of the priests
Glyphs whose sound is their word's opening
Glyphs with traditional sounds: the sounds of the first codex, known to scribes
a face put on, a god worn
Every syllable Ki'i'chek uses, and the glyphs that write it
The numbers: the shell for zero, then bar and dot; then the places of the count
Compounds: the first glyph is usually the head, and those after it modify it
the whole round: the sun's day, the soul's existence
One run, several readings: context decides how the glyphs group
the elder man of the household
a man of the great house: a nobleman
a man standing on the roof of his house
Names written in sounds, a scribe's skill: a closing consonant takes a syllable whose vowel is silent
cha-ku-l(u): the last vowel is silent
